bibliography.checked_against: the article's first page (running head) and the MTAK repository record
bibliography.note: the page prints the journal only as 'Annal. Biol. Tihany 27 183–191, Hungária 1960'; MTAK records it as 'A Magyar Tudományos Akadémia Tihanyi Biológiai Kutatóintézetének Évkönyve' 27: 183–191 (ISSN 0365-3005). Author Elek Woynárovich; title as in the entry (the page writes '0,5 to 28° C'). Received 3 March 1960.

claims.claim: Routine oxygen uptake of unfed pike larvae rose with a Q10 of about 2.4–2.6 between 5 and 25 °C (project calculation)
claims.quote: Pike larva … Freshly-hatched I … 5,6 … II … 5,7 … III … 6,6
claims.conditions: O₂ uptake per g dry mass (mg/h) of yolk-sac to ready-to-feed (not yet fed) pike larvae, 3–30 larvae per vessel, 2-h closed-vessel incubations, Winkler O₂; larvae held at 10–20 °C, then 1–2 h at each test temperature (0.5, 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 28 °C); 1958–59
claims.note: Table 3 gives the 25 °C ÷ 5 °C ratio (Woynárovich labels it Q20): 5.6, 5.7, 6.6 for stages I, II, III; it matches Table 2 (1.23/0.22, 4.13/0.72, 7.41/1.12). Q10 = ratio^(10/20) = 2.37, 2.39, 2.57 → 2.4–2.6. The rates are short-term responses (1–2 h at each temperature; the author found 10 min and 2 h gave the same result and judged that sufficient 'for their adaptation'), not rates after days of acclimation; saying so would help the reader

claims.paper: §5.8 (lesson 'An adult set cannot grow a larva')
claims.claim: the adult pike set's respiration Q10 (1.73) is shallower than a larva's (2.5; Woynárovich 1960)
claims.location: p. 187 (PDF p. 5), Table 3; p. 184 (PDF p. 2), methods
claims.quote: this period having proved to be sufficient for their adaptation
claims.conditions: as above: per g dry mass, pre-feeding larvae, 1–2 h at each test temperature
claims.note: 2.5 lies within the stages' 2.37–2.57 (2.57 for larvae ready to feed). The comparison sets a short-exposure larval Q10 against an adult set fitted on acclimated fish; the source does not test acclimation beyond 2 h, so the rewrite should state the exposure time

claims.quote: Pike larva … Before beginning to feed III … 6,6
claims.conditions: stage III: 'larvae respiring through the gills, the yolk substance already consumed but before they begin to food' (Summary, p. 190); 5 → 25 °C
claims.note: 6.6^0.5 = 2.57 for the ready-to-feed stage (2.4 at hatching); 2.5 is a fair round value. Not measured on feeding larvae, and only over 1–2-h exposures

notes: Other values: per-100-larvae O₂ uptake (Table 1) and dry masses (100 larvae: 0.205 g at hatching, 0.169 g ready to feed; total length 8.55–12.7 mm). Uptake per g dry mass rose 4.5× from hatching to the ready-to-feed stage at a given temperature. Pike larvae tolerated 5 °C at first but died after 4–6 h at it later in development; the author judged 10–15 °C best for pike larvae and saw 'disadvantageous' changes above 21 °C (Fig. 1). Sheat-fish (wels) Table 3 stage III reads 7.7 though Table 2 gives 6.90/0.86 = 8.0 (not used by the paper).
